purpose: Ivermectin is used to treat certain parasitic infections in the body, such as river blindness, strongyloidiasis (a type of intestinal worm), scabies, and head lice. It works against a variety of parasites and is available in oral tablet form as well as topical creams and lotions for skin conditions. Your doctor will prescribe it based on the specific infection you have.
how_it_works: Ivermectin works by paralyzing and killing parasites. It does this by interfering with the nervous system and muscle function of the parasite, causing them to become paralyzed and eventually die. Human cells are not affected in the same way, which is why it is safe for us to use at the right doses.
common_side_effects: You might experience dizziness, nausea, diarrhea, stomach pain, or mild skin rash. Some people feel tired or get a mild headache. If treating a skin condition with the cream or lotion, you may notice some skin irritation, dryness, or a burning feeling at the application site.
warnings: Do not use ivermectin without a prescription and medical supervision — taking the wrong dose can be dangerous. Avoid the version sold for animals, as it is NOT safe for humans. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or have liver problems. If you develop severe dizziness, swelling, difficulty breathing, or vision changes, seek medical help right away. It is not proven safe or effective for viral infections like COVID-19.
typical_dosing: The dose depends on your weight and what condition is being treated. For most parasitic infections, it is taken as a single oral dose or a short course of doses. Your doctor will calculate the exact amount that is right for you. Always take it on an empty stomach with a full glass of water, and follow your doctor's instructions carefully.
